idiom_name: Express res.format handlers + res.render view engines
implementation_notes: res.format() is the negotiation point: it inspects req.accepts() and runs the matching handler, so one route renders HTML with res.render() through the engine registered by app.set('view engine')/app.engine(), returns JSON with res.json(), and streams CSV or PDF from the very same model object. The engine map plus the handler table replaces the classic view registry, and no view object is instantiated per request. Keep the attached-observer form only when one server pushes updates to several live representations (SSE/WebSocket fan-out), where an explicit subscriber list is clearer than re-rendering per request.
pitfalls: res.format sets Content-Type from the matched key, so an html handler that returns JSON sends text/html and clients mis-parse; set the type explicitly for non-obvious formats.
Express 5 throws for unhandled formats while Express 4 falls through to default: without a default handler the client gets an empty 406 that hides the mismatch.
View engines are registered on the app instance (app.engine/app.set), so tests that register engines leak into later suites unless each test builds its own app.
